name: Synthwave, a supplemental Digital and 3D Aesthetics reference. The source collection does not directly name this style.
visualIdentity: Evokes 1980s electronic-music imagery: neon night colors, perspective grids, striped sunsets, and selected mountain or sports-car silhouettes. Related to Retrofuturism but not interchangeable with it.
suitableUses: Source-suggested uses are music videos, lyric visualizers, and retro event promos. Inferred fit includes titles and themed intros. Suitability for other topics is unspecified.
limitations: VHS treatment is optional and must not cause persistent corruption; scanlines alone do not represent VHS. Avoid vaporwave or cyberpunk layering and flashing on every beat. Some source details were not verified against the source video.
palette: Suggested tokens, not supplied: background #171333, foreground #F8ECDC, accents #E05AAA, #5DCEE0, and #EEA15D. Task or brand colors override them. Gradients are optional and limited to sunset or atmosphere; grid lines and text stay discrete. Foreground on background measures 15.308:1, so verify composited frames.
motionAndInteraction: Movement drives toward a clear horizon in sync with musical sections; suggested grid-speed and camera-height changes land on verified beats. Video motion must derive from seekable time. Interactive delivery may add a suggested reduced-motion mode. Optional motion-012 and motion-015 apply only if scene screening supports them; selecting neither is valid.
audio: The style assigns no genre, tempo, instrument, or voice. Suggested direction is music-synchronized horizon movement with section-based changes. Voiceover and sung vocals are unspecified. Honor task audio requirements first, and verify speech intelligibility and absence of clipping.
assetRequirements: The source does not list required assets. Inferred needs include Three.js geometry for roads, grids, and vehicles, GLSL shaders for sky and sunset, and loaded fonts for SVG or DOM text. Authorized audio is required for any soundtrack. Silhouettes are optional.
combinations: Style-105 suits section-synchronized horizon timing for music videos and retro promos. Style-093 suits lyric and title typography. Keep gradients to sunsets, keep grid lines discrete, and avoid persistent VHS corruption. Do not combine with vaporwave or cyberpunk aesthetics.
productionApproach: Three.js and GLSL render the scene, and SVG or DOM render text. GSAP's paused timeline supplies seekable time. HyperFrames is the default pipeline; Remotion is a fallback only if HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limitation exists. Chroma-js validates contrast, and rendered frames must be inspected before delivery.
